request:
Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Can one student borrow the same book more than once at the same time, and is there a limit on how many books one student can have out at once?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should the librarian be the only one who can add books, and do students need to log in, or is typing their name enough (what if two students share the same name)?
A: No, they just give their name.
Q: Is there a due date or time limit for borrowing, and should the librarian be able to see who has which book, edit a book's copy count, or remove a book?
A: Not needed for now.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).

import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import app as appmod

client = TestClient(appmod.app)


def new(copies=1):
    r = client.post("/books", json={"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies": copies})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    return r.json()


def test_add_and_list_and_get():
    b = new(2)
    assert b["available"] == 2
    assert any(x["id"] == b["id"] for x in client.get("/books").json())
    r = client.get(f"/books/{b['id']}")
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["title"] == "T"
    assert client.get("/books/99999").status_code == 404


def test_validation():
    assert client.post("/books", json={"title": "", "author": "A", "copies": 1}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/books", json={"title": "T", "author": "A", "copies": -1}).status_code == 422
    assert client.post("/books", json={"title": "T"}).status_code == 422
    b = new()
    assert client.post(f"/books/{b['id']}/borrow", json={"student": " "}).status_code == 422


def test_borrow_return():
    b = new(1)
    i = b["id"]
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/return", json={"student": "Ann"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/borrow", json={"student": "Ann"}).status_code == 201
    assert client.get(f"/books/{i}").json()["available"] == 0
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/borrow", json={"student": "Bob"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/return", json={"student": "Bob"}).status_code == 409
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/return", json={"student": "Ann"}).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"/books/{i}").json()["available"] == 1
    assert client.post(f"/books/{i}/borrow", json={"student": "Bob"}).status_code == 201
    assert client.post("/books/99999/borrow", json={"student": "Bob"}).status_code == 404

`app.py` is written and my three tests in `tests/test_app.py` pass. They cover adding, listing and viewing books, input checks, and borrowing and returning. Data is kept in `library.db`, which is created when the app starts.

- **`POST /books`** adds a book from `{title, author, copies}`. Title and author can't be blank and copies must be at least 1, otherwise it returns 422.
- **`GET /books`** lists all books. Each one shows `id`, `title`, `author`, `copies` and `available`, which is how many are still on the shelf.
- **`GET /books/{id}`** shows one book, or returns 404 if there is no such book.
- **`POST /books/{id}/borrow`** takes `{student}`. It returns 409 when every copy is out, and 422 if the name is blank.
- **`POST /books/{id}/return`** takes `{student}`. It returns 409 if that student hasn't borrowed the book.

You left two things open, so I chose the simplest option for each. A student can borrow the same book more than once at the same time, and there is no limit on how many books one student has out. Students are identified only by the name they type, so two students with the same name count as the same person when returning.
